text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Z$210 million Boka Tobacco Auction Floors opened in Harare on Tuesday with the first bale of tobacco being sold at U.S.$4.10 a kilogram.

- The British government on Tuesday banned Air Zimbabwe's scheduled flights to London's Gatwick Airport in retaliation to Zimbabwe's refusal to allow the fourth British Airways weekly flight from Harare to fly north on the same day.

- Kenyan president Daniel arap Moi arrives in Harare on Wednesday morning on a four-day state visit during which he will officially open the Zimbabwe International Trade Fair in the southern city of Bulawayo.
- Africa's troubled spots, with Zaire topping the list, will dominate the Organisation of African Unity summit to be held in Harare in June, OAU secretary-general Salim Ahmed Salim said on Wednesday.
